questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The climate, the culture and meeting new people

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of information, which at times were a bit difficult to navigate in. It was nice that it was a "real person" sending the information who was good at answering questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think there were a lot of events and stuff you could join and the university made a good effort to make you feel welcome. I did not get any assistance really, but I had the feeling I could get it if I needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different student accommodation opportunities on campus. Queen Mary Building was the only one offering guaranteed housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A really big common kitchen at the accommodation

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is really expensive compared to what you get, and you should expect to pay a lot more than advertised. They charge a lot of extra fees for almost everything, like extra cleaning fees, transaction fees. The facilities are generally poor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It takes some time understanding the process as it is rather different from what you're used to. But there is help to get, so it just takes some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An employee at the University sent you e-mails with all the relevant information and was also there to help you through the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got 4 out of the 8 or 10 classes I applied for, and it was not possible to change.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it step by step and ask for help

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were pretty difficult for an exchange student. As a law student from a civil law country, it would have been nice with more introduction to the common law system etc. or maybe the opportunity to take BA classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more student involvement and participation

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporations Law, Race and the Law, Evidence and Interpretation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Race and the Law was a good class to get to know some people, because you get involved with other students and you learn about Australian history and society

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There's a surcharge on everything and when you pay high amounts as for example your rent it gets considerably higher. The student accommodations make you pay extra fees for using a foreign card etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I didn't buy any of the books, because it didn't really seem necessary. Food is a bit cheaper than Denmark, but nightlife is way more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really join anything, but there were a lot of opportunities to do it

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different kinds, both academic, athletic and social

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It's a good way to meet other exchange students to live in student housing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and drive to the many destinations around Sydney

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In general, I mostly connected with other exchange students, as I only met the local students in class, where there weren't an opportunity to talk.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very kind and helpful people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There's a lot of planning which can seem overwhelming, but as soon as you get there you forget it. 
Enjoy having more free time and see and travel as much possible
But also take your time for yourself when you need it, you won't miss anything from that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The classes seem way more difficult in the beginning, but the professors are generally really nice and there's a lot of help available if it's difficult to get it all done

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing Australia and meeting a lot of new people in new circumstances

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam periods are pretty stressfull

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
